per_view.notes: Slender light-grey fuselage with distinct front upper-deck hump and tall swept dark-blue fin plus horizontal stabilizers. Passenger window line and cockpit windows present. Nose gear and main-gear bogies visible. Engines read as blocky shapes clustered against the belly, not four clearly separated underwing nacelles. Wings largely edge-on in this side view.

Slender white fuselage with distinct front-third upper hump and cockpit region. Swept dark-blue tail fin. Passenger window line and blue cheatline present. Engine nacelles read but appear bunched near the wing root/belly rather than spread outboard on clear pylons. Nose and main gear trucks visible below.

Head-on: four dark-inlet nacelles under swept wings with dihedral, plausible spacing. Rounded nose with bulged crown reads as hump/cockpit. Tall blue vertical fin; thin horizontal stabilizer visible. Central cluster of blocky main-gear trucks plus nose gear. Light-grey body, coherent. No window lines visible from this angle.

Rear head-on: four dark-inlet nacelles evenly spaced under wings. Vertical fin is a very thin dark stick, too narrow. Horizontal stabilizers sit oddly high near the hump. Wings are thin flat boards, little dihedral or visible taper. Nose+main gear clusters visible under body. All-grey body, no windows visible from this angle.

Four grey nacelles, two per swept tapering wing, but clustered inboard with little forward offset. Slender tapered fuselage with dashed window line and a dark oval (upper-deck/window hint). Swept vertical fin and horizontal stabilizers present. Clean light-body/grey-wing livery, no floating parts. Hump not readable from top.

Slender white fuselage with rounded nose, swept tapering wings with dihedral, tall dark-blue swept fin and horizontal stabilizers. Blue cheatline and window row present. No distinct 747 upper-deck hump; nose crown is nearly flat. Four engine-like nacelles but several hang near the belly, some appear floating/misplaced. Nose and small main gear visible. Reads as a generic airliner, not clearly a 74

Slender white fuselage with tapered tail cone and a partial front upper-deck hump. Tall swept blue fin plus horizontal stabilizers. Swept grey wings. Engines and main-gear wheels cluster ambiguously under the belly/wing roots rather than four clean pylon-hung nacelles under the wings. Window line and blue stripe present.

Grey 747 with front upper-deck hump, dark-blue window line and swept navy tail. Four underwing nacelles present but chunky; forward-left engine reads as a floating barrel. Nose gear plus multi-wheel main-gear clusters visible. Swept wings with dihedral, tapering nose/tail. Engine mounts look slightly detached.

White fuselage with grey swept wings, dark-blue cabin stripe and dashed window line plus small cockpit-triangle windows. Four grey underwing nacelles on pylons visible across both wings. Nose gear and main-gear trucks present. Upper-deck hump exists but is short and shallow, blending quickly; reads as a subtle bump rather than the iconic 747 crown. Tall swept fin present.
